brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Four full hex bases (piece refs at 0,0 / 1,0 / -1,0 / 0,1 level 0) joined by joint bolts; check_build ok, meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator has no load model and cannot verify a 50 kg rating; the printed PETG parts and M6 joints have not been load-tested. Nothing in the build establishes this rating.
Two notch drawers (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) at cells -1,1 and 0,-1, each between touching bases. A third was placed and removed to leave exactly two.

finish.summary: Built a small shelf unit: four full hex bases (the shelving, at levels 0 around cells 0,0 / 1,0 / -1,0 / 0,1), two notch drawers (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf, one at -1,1 and one at 0,-1) set between touching bases, with the open faces capped and joints bolted (lockJoints). check_build is clean with meshClash clear. Overall footprint about 524 x 80 x 545 mm. The 50 kg book rating cannot be verified: the configurator checks fit and collisions only and knows nothing about load, PETG strength or creep, so I did not claim it. Printed PETG with M6 bolts is the user's material choice to assess, and the bolt notes call for hand-tightening only.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
